e_abnahme_kette: After a green review, request merge automatically
e_abnahme_kette_h: After a green review the merge request goes to the person in charge automatically – if the lead has given merge approval for the task. Otherwise the AMW asks the lead.
e_pruefstufen_h: On: AMW rates each review request by the changed files. High (database, sign-in, permissions, file exchange …) is reviewed by the lead, medium by another agent; low – docs and tests only – needs no review request if a green full run checked exactly this commit.
e_release_takt_h: When AMW reports that something can be released (green review, merge approval, full run on exactly this commit). It never releases by itself – the message goes to whoever handles merges, otherwise to the lead.
e_plan_automatik_h: On: AMW updates the plan to what happens. When an agent starts a run for one of its tasks that has not started yet, the task is set to “running” (task from the run, “A1234” in the description or the branch). If the task is waiting for someone, it stays as it is. After a release (amw release ausliefern), every included task with merge approval is set to done, and so is a task whose number starts the title of a merged GitHub PR (“A1234: …”, or “closes A1234” in its text) with green checks.
e_neue_aufgaben_h: Into the milestone: the lead names the milestone when creating a task (as before). Into the inbox: new tasks without a milestone wait in the inbox until the lead deliberately pulls them into a milestone; naming a milestone when creating puts them straight into it.
e_meilenstein_fertig_h: When all tasks of a milestone are done: suggest = the lead gets a notice and closes it; automatic = AMW closes it itself. If a version is mandatory and missing, it stays a suggestion.
eg_h: New tasks land here. The lead deliberately pulls them into a milestone: amw aufgabe aendern <no> --bogen <no>.
gs_h: Each part of the service reports after every round. If one stays silent longer than allowed, AMW restarts it and tells you once.
gs_alt: The service has stopped reporting – is it still running?
anl_h: Each cost increase of a session belongs to the wake-ups in the same period (several share it); without a wake-up it counts as own work. Avoidable: the agent did not have to do anything.
anl_nachlesen: After {n} of {w} wake-ups the agent read up again within 2 minutes ({p} %).
anl_nachlesen_leer: Reading up after wake-ups is measured from now on.

anl_je_weckruf_1: Cost per wake-up on the day before {v}: {a} $, on the day after: {b} $
anl_leer: No measurements in this period yet.
bn_unterwegs: Saved – the PC applies it shortly

g_fehlt: The log of this session no longer exists.

pjw_wie_0: You think it through with the co-developer in chat; they create the topics in the AMW.|A reviewer reads each topic; you settle objections and approve each topic.|“Complete concept” starts the rough planning.
pjw_wie_1: The AMW starts a planner (headless, thorough model) with all approved topics.|It looks for duplicates, oversized and unclear topics and proposes milestones.|You write notes, it revises – every version stays visible.|Your yes fixes the rough plan and creates the milestones.
pjw_wie_2: The AMW starts the planner for the next milestone.|It splits it into packages and picks who carries them out.|You approve the plan as one block – that starts the delivery.
pjw_wie_3: The AMW hands out the packages, agents work, every package is checked automatically.|You only answer real questions – the lead asks them with a recommendation.|What is running right now is shown on the overview.
pjw_wie_4: Full test, then a checker compares the milestone with the concept and prepares the demo.|You accept or request rework.|Then the AMW plans the next milestone in detail; steps 3 to 5 repeat.
